<Rep. Jamie Raskin>: H.R. 38, the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act, would supplant the judgment, authority, and autonomy of each state to set their own standards for who may carry a concealed firearm within the state and instead would require states to accept the standards set by the most lenient states, some of which have no standards at all.
Every element of the title of this bill is wrong. This bill has nothing to do with ``reciprocity.'' States that right now want to engage in reciprocity arrangements with other states for concealed carry policies have that absolute right. Forty states have enacted some form of concealed carry reciprocity, exercising their powers under the Second Amendment and the Tenth Amendment to negotiate reciprocal recognition agreements with neighboring states or all of the states.\1\ Twenty-nine of those states do not require any permit at all.\2\ Ten states have chosen not to engage in any concealed carry reciprocity arrangements.\3\ These policy decisions are completely up to the states. But this bill would abolish this voluntary reciprocity right that the states currently enjoy.
\1\Permits/Licenses That the State Listed at Left Honors, Handgunlaw.us (Aug. 8, 2025) https://www.handgunlaw.us/states/ USStatesMyStateHonors.pdf.
\2\Concealed Carry, Giffords (last visited Aug. 21, 2025) https:// giffords.org/lawcenter/gun-laws/policy-areas/guns-in-public/concealed-carry/.
\3\Permits/Licenses That the State Listed at Left Honors, Handgunlaw.us (Aug. 8, 2025) https://www.handgunlaw.us/states/ USStatesMyStateHonors.pdf.
This legislation would substitute the judgment and autonomy of each state legislature to set their own standards for who may carry a concealed firearm with the standards set only by the most lenient states. This bill is therefore not about voluntary reciprocity. It is a nationwide mandate that our colleagues would impose on every single state, forcing them to accept the public safety risks of states with the most permissive and ineffectual gun safety laws.
There is also nothing ``constitutional'' about this legislation. Under the Tenth and Second Amendments, police powers authorize states to choose concealed carry laws consistent with their own traditions, with American traditions, and local public safety. This is the meaning of the Bruen decision in 2022 by the Supreme Court.\4\
\4\N.Y. State Rifle & Pistol Ass'n v. Bruen, 597 U.S. 1 (2022).
States have exercised that power to determine for themselves who may carry a concealed firearm. For example, in my State of Maryland, we have stringent requirements to legally carry a concealed firearm.\5\ You need a permit and to get one, you must complete safety training which includes instruction on self-defense, safe firearm storage, conflict de-escalation, and suicide prevention--and then you have to demonstrate that you can shoot accurately and handle a gun safely. You must also store your firearms in accordance with Maryland's Child Access Prevention law. And you must be at least 21 years old. But there are 29 states that do not require a permit, background check, or safety training to carry a concealed firearm in most places, and some states allow you to carry a concealed gun as young as 18 years old. This legislation would allow someone who comes from one of these states to come to Maryland and carry a concealed firearm contrary to the laws adopted by the elected representatives of millions of people.
\5\Concealed Carry in Maryland, Giffords (Dec. 31, 2023), https:// giffords.org/lawcenter/state-laws/concealed-carry-in-maryland/.
This nationwide, straitjacket mandate makes it possible for dangerous people from one state to circumvent the laws of every other state. For example, a person who cannot meet the requirements of Maryland law, either because they fail the live-fire accuracy test, or because there are indicators that they are a danger to themselves or other people, would be able to shop around for a state whose standards they could meet.
There are many states that previously required a permit to carry a concealed firearm and later dropped their permit requirement but still issue optional permits so that permitholders can take advantage of reciprocity agreements and for other purposes. Arizona is one such state--and it makes no distinction between Arizona residents and all other U.S. citizens who apply for a concealed carry permit in Arizona.\6\ Arizona also does not require an in-person application.\7\ So, under this legislation, a person who lives in Maryland but could not obtain a Maryland concealed carry permit, could get a permit from Arizona without ever setting foot in the state, and suddenly be allowed to concealed carry in Maryland and every other state in the nation--even though they might have shown signs of dangerousness.
\6\Concealed Carry in Arizona, Giffords (Dec. 31, 2023), https:// giffords.org/lawcenter/state-laws/concealed-carry-in-arizona/.
\7\Arizona Concealed Carry Reciprocity Map & Gun Laws, USCCA (Mar. 31, 2025) https://www.usconcealedcarry.com/resources/ ccw_reciprocity_map/az-gun-laws/.
And to make this race to the bottom even more shocking, the bill specifically allows such a person to carry a concealed gun in a gun-free school zone. This bill would erode not only our state laws, but our federal laws protecting students, teachers, and others in our public and private schools.
The end result of all of this is clear: we will all be less safe. Studies have found that weak concealed carry laws are associated with a 15% increase in violent crime\8\ and 11% higher rates of homicides using handguns.\9\ This bill would cause those weak laws to have dangerous nationwide repercussions. This bill would almost certainly lead to nationwide increases in violent crime and homicide--reversing the progress of the last two years, which have featured historic reductions in violent crime\10\ and homicide.\11\
\8\John H. Donohue, Abhay Aneja, and Kyle D. Weber, Right-to-carry Laws and Violent Crime: A Comprehensive Assessment Using Panel Data and a State-level Synthetic Control Analysis, J. of Empirical Leg. Stud. 16, no. 2 (2019).
\9\Michael Siegel, Easiness of Legal Access to Concealed Firearm Permits and Homicide Rates in the United States, Am. J. Public Health 107, no. 12 (2017) available at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/ PMC5678379/.
\10\Alexander Mallin, FBI's latest data shows `historic' drop in crime: Garland, ABC News (June 10, 2024), https://abcnews.go.com/ Politics/fbis-latest-data-show-historic-drop-crime-garland/ story?id=110989589.
\11\Bill Hutchinson, US poised to see dramatic drop in homicides for 3rd straight year, ABC News (Dec. 31, 2024) https://abcnews.go.com/ US/united-states-drop-homicides-2024/story?id=116902123.
Given the increased public safety risks that this legislation would impose on all of our states, law enforcement officers and law enforcement organizations across America strongly oppose this legislation.\12\ They know that this bill would create serious risks and would make their jobs more difficult and more dangerous. If this bill were to become law, law enforcement would have to deal with even more armed individuals, and this bill would restrict their ability to arrest or detain a person who is carrying a concealed firearm. Law enforcement officers who keep our communities safe will be unable to know the permit requirements of all 50 states, and unable to determine whether someone is lawfully carrying a firearm, since the bill allows people to carry across state lines without any permit at all if they live in a permitless carry state. And any mistakes an officer makes in trying to enforce the law could subject that officer to a lawsuit under this bill. As a statement from seven law enforcement organizations--including the International Association of Chiefs of Police, the Law Enforcement Action Partnership, and the Association of Prosecuting Attorneys--explains, ``this mandate would severely erode public and officer safety'' and make it ``near impossible for law enforcement to confirm that an armed individual is carrying legally.''\13\
\12\Statement of National Law Enforcement Organizations on Proposed Concealed Carry Mandate available at https://www.congress.gov/119/ meeting/house/118065/documents/HMKP-119-JU00-20250325-SD008.pdf.
\13\Id.
During H.R. 38's markup, Committee Democrats offered several amendments aimed at limiting the significant safety risks posed by this legislation. We offered amendments to prevent people from carrying a concealed firearm under this legislation if: they were convicted of committing a crime against a law enforcement officer; they were subject to a restraining order for stalking, threats, or harassment; or they were convicted of a violent misdemeanor. We also offered amendments to prevent H.R. 38 from overriding states' own concealed carry laws within their borders. The Majority rejected all of these amendments.
This bill reflects the Republican agenda when it comes to public safety: more guns, in more places. If that really worked, the United States would already be the safest place in the world. But it isn't. There are about 400 million guns in the United States--more guns than people.\14\ The firearm homicide rate in the U.S. is nearly 25 times higher than other high-income countries, and the firearm suicide rate is nearly 10 times that of other high-income countries.\15\
\14\Christopher Ingraham, There are more guns than people in the United States, according to a new study of global firearm ownership, Wash. Post (June 19, 2018), https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wonk/ wp/2018/06/19/there-are-more-guns-than-people-in-the-united-states-according-to-a-new-study-of-global-firearm-ownership/.
\15\Erin Grinshteyn & David Hemenway, Violent death rates in the US compared to those of the other high-income countries, 2015, Preventive Medicine, Vol. 123, 20-26 (2019) available at https:// pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30817955/.
Finally, I must note that as our Republican colleagues are advancing this dangerous legislation, the Trump Administration is taking many more actions that will make life easier for violent criminals. They pardoned more than 1,500 convicted insurrectionists, and they are trying to rollback regulations designed to reduce gun trafficking and illegal gun sales.\16\ They are also working to give convicted criminals the right to own a gun again.\17\ And it was reported that they plan to cut as many as 1,000 agents--more than a third--from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, or ATF.\18\ If Republicans get their way, we will not only have more people-- potentially including convicted criminals--carrying a lot more guns in all of our states, but we will have drastically fewer federal agents left to investigate and prevent gun crimes. This puts all of our communities at risk.
\16\Exec. Order No. 14,206 (Feb. 7, 2025) https:// www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/02/protecting-second-amendment-rights/.
\17\Application for Relief From Disabilities Imposed by Federal Laws With Respect to the Acquisition, Receipt, Transfer, Shipment, Transportation, or Possession of Firearms, 90 Fed. Reg. 34394 (July 22, 2025).
\18\Evan Perez and Hannah Rabinowitz, Patel plans major cutback to ATF by moving as many as 1,000 agents to FBI, CNN (Mar. 22, 2025), https://www.cnn.com/2025/03/22/politics/atf-agents-fbi/index.html.
I urge my colleagues to oppose this dangerous legislation.
Jamie Raskin,
Ranking Member.
